cards.text: The remnant of Judah asked Jeremiah the prophet to find out what the LORD wanted them to do, and they promised to obey, pleasant or unpleasant (Jeremiah 42:1-6). The LORD's answer was clear: stay in the land, don't be afraid of the king of Babylon, and do NOT go to Egypt (Jeremiah 42:10-19). Now Jeremiah has finished telling them every word the LORD sent him to say.

cards.question: Then Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men answer Jeremiah. What do they tell him?

cards.text: Friend, they ASKED for this answer (Jeremiah 42:2-3). Now they claim the LORD never sent Jeremiah to say, 'You must not go to Egypt to reside there.'

Then they say Baruch son of Neriah, Jeremiah's own scribe (Jeremiah 36:32), is inciting Jeremiah against them. That's like the doctor telling you to cut back on cookies, and you decide the NURSE must have put him up to it.

cards.question: The men claim Baruch wants them handed over to the Chaldeans, the people of Babylon, so they'll be put to ___ or exiled to Babylon.
After all that, Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces obey the LORD's command to stay in the land of Judah.
Johanan son of Kareah and the commanders of the forces don't stay in Judah. Who do they take with them?

cards.text: Even people who had come back to Judah from the nations where they'd been scattered. Men, women, children, the king's daughters, and everyone Nebuzaradan, Babylon's captain of the guard, had let stay with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the man the king of Babylon had appointed over the cities of Judah (Jeremiah 40:5).

cards.question: Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah go along with the group.
The whole group enters the land of Egypt. How far do they go?

cards.text: All the way to Tahpanhes, and the text says why: they did not obey the voice of the LORD. That's like typing the address into the GPS YOURSELF and then ignoring every single turn.
Egypt may be a long way from home, but the LORD isn't finished with this crowd. Right there in Tahpanhes, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah.

cards.question: The LORD gives Jeremiah something to do while the Jews in Tahpanhes watch. What is it?

answers.text: Bury large stones in the pavement
Break a clay jar by the gate
Wear a yoke through the streets

cards.question: The LORD tells Jeremiah to bury the stones in the clay of the brick pavement at the entrance to ___ palace at Tahpanhes.
Then the LORD gives Jeremiah a message for the people about those stones. The LORD of Hosts says He will send for someone. Who?

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The very king they were afraid of (Jeremiah 42:11), and the LORD calls him His servant.

cards.question: What does the LORD say He will set over the stones buried at Pharaoh's palace?

cards.text: His THRONE, and he'll spread his royal pavilion over those same stones. That's like dodging your boss all week, finally finding a quiet spot, and your boss walks in and moves his desk right there.

cards.question: According to the LORD, Egypt will be a safe place from the king of Babylon.

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar will come and strike down the land of Egypt, bringing death, captivity and the sword, each to those destined for it. This one's heavy, friend, because the LORD had warned that the sword they feared would overtake them there (Jeremiah 42:16).

cards.question: The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar will ___ the temples of the gods of Egypt and take their gods as captives.

cards.text: The LORD says He will kindle that fire Himself. Then Nebuchadnezzar will wrap himself with the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment.

cards.question: The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar will leave Egypt unscathed.

cards.text: He will demolish the sacred pillars of the temple of the sun and burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt. That's where we'll pause with the remnant, friend, and their story keeps on rolling.
